title: Occultist
name: Alhazred
description: The Occultist is a scholar of the psyche whose own mind carries a passenger: the black-beast, a thing from the Outer Spheres that lends him its power and at times borrows his voice. Through it he hexes, binds and heals, though his powers are not always reliable. He has gone further into the unknown than anyone should, and despite his remorse, has not lost his appetite for it.
history: The Occultist was a respected scholar and, in private, the teacher of a small circle of followers who gathered on astrologically favoured nights to send their spirits out beyond the world. In the Outer Spheres he came upon a pyramid, and something in its halls called to him. To make room, he carved out parts of his mind, but in a séance to welcome it, he realised what he had invited. At the cost of his students' lives, he kept most of it out, but when he left home, he didn't do so alone.
summary: A courteous scholar of the psyche who shares his mind with an eldritch passenger, and still hungers for what lies beyond.

appearance.hairColor: Black, without a trace of grey
appearance.features: Lined face, short black goatee, and a waxed moustache curled at the tips

clothing.head: Cream turban, wound close
clothing.body: Long brown robe with wide, flared sleeves, trimmed in a red-and-black lattice pattern, over a dark tunic
clothing.legs: Covered by the robe, which falls to the ankles
clothing.accessories: Gold medallion necklace, yellow sash with his dagger thrust through it, scrolls tucked at the hip

magic: Eldritch power from the Outer Spheres, lent by the black-beast: hexes, grasping tentacles, and healing
notes: A scholar of the mind, and he speaks like one: of psyches, auras and mental states, of fear as something to be reasoned away, and of magic as what a disciplined mind can reach
No armchair scholar: he has crossed deserts by caravan, lived among the peoples he studied, and knows distant lands and customs from his travels
Lonely despite his passenger, though his lecturing and his corrections, especially of the unlearned, tend to push people away
At times the black-beast speaks through him, always in capitals and often in its own guttural tongue ("AS'KARAKH NOMARAGH"), and refers to the Occultist in the third person, as "CH'TROG"
Despite his age, his hair is still fully black, and he waxes and curls his moustache daily
